text:
maria: Heads-up — we started seeing a steady rise in CE counts across multiple us-east racks ~08:22 UTC. Capacity available for new jobs dropped ~12% and provisioning is getting rate-limited by autoscaler. :eyes:

simon: Which racks exactly? any pattern by rack or GPU SKU?

maria: Mostly rack-us-e-08 and rack-us-e-11. Mix of A10G and A30 nodes. Not single-card, looks like multiple cards per host incrementing CE counters.

priya: Can you paste the logs/snippet? also curious if nvlink/psu logs show anything.

maria: Logs attached inline:
```
[2025-06-14T08:21:12Z] gpu0 CE_counter += 7 (driver=520.61)
[2025-06-14T08:21:13Z] nv-host0: no link flaps
[2025-06-14T08:21:15Z] gpu1 CE_counter += 5
[2025-06-14T08:21:18Z] kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: gpu reset request
[2025-06-14T08:21:19Z] provisioning: pod create throttled by quota
```

matt-oncall: infra-bot alert came through: "gpu-health-monitor: correctable-error-rate > 300% baseline in us-east for last 5m" — I put the relevant hosts in soft-quarantine (no new jobs) at 08:27.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-health-monitor detected CE rate anomaly in cluster=us-east, hosts=12, severity=high. Auto-quarantine applied to hosts: rack-us-e-08-[01..06], rack-us-e-11-[01..06].

lee: :thumbsup: Good call on quarantine. Any obvious correlation with recent driver/firmware changes?

maria: No driver rollouts this week. Last infra change was a small kernel backport on 2025-06-10. We'll rule that out but need to test.

simon: Can we run remote diagnostics and nvml memtest on 2 hosts to repro? If CE increments persist under idle, that's telling.

priya: I'm running nvml diagnostics on rack-us-e-08-03 and -11-02 now. Will report in 5m.

vendor-monitor: Received telemetry from vendor: looks like a batch of cards with elevated CE rates shipped to our us-east PO. They recommend firmware checksum verification and an extended ECC scrub pass.

maria: If vendor is flagging a batch, let's avoid broad replacements yet. Short term plan: keep soft-quarantine, divert new allocations to us-west, run targeted ECC scrub + nvml memtest, collect kernel reset stacks.

matt-oncall: Agreed. Also need cost note — diverting to us-west will increase egress and spot cost by ~8-12% for next 24h. Flagging finance for visibility.

lee: If diagnostics confirm hardware cohort, we'll schedule cross-rack swap with spares and open RMA with vendor. Prioritize prod-critical pools first.

priya: Diagnostics: both hosts show CE counters rising under light load during memtest. NVML returns corrected errors, no permanent hangs so far.

simon: That matches vendor pattern. New action: rollback planned provisioning for new pods into affected racks (already soft-quarantine), escalate to hardware team to qualify RMAs, and enable continuous ECC-scrub job on quarantined hosts.

maria: I'm creating an incident ticket and adding the vendor & hw tags. Also enabling a temporary autoscaler override to ignore those hosts so we don't chase capacity and cause provisioning thrash.

matt-oncall: I'll update the oncall runbook and post a short notice to #customers-ops if SLA-backed capacity could be impacted.

lee: TL;DR action items: 1) keep soft-quarantine + divert allocations, 2) run ECC-scrub & nvml memtest, 3) collect kernel reset stacks and upload to incident ticket, 4) engage vendor RMA if scrub doesn't reduce CE, 5) finance notified about cost delta.

maria: I'll follow up with the scrub results in ~1h. For now retaining quarantines. :hammer:
